Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: Work done by the leak in 1 hour = 1 - 3 = 1 . 2 7 14 Leak will empty the tank in 14 hrs.

Pipes and Cistern.question: 4. Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 37 minutes and 45 minutes respectively. Both pipes are opened. The cistern will be filled in just half an hour, if the B is turned off after:
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: Let B be turned off after x minutes. Then, Part filled by (A + B) in x min. + Part filled by A in (30 -x) min. = 1. x 2 + 1 + (30 - x). 2 = 1 75 45 75 11x + (60 -2x) = 1 225 75 11x + 180 - 6x = 225. x = 9.

Pipes and Cistern.question: 5. A tank is filled by three pipes with uniform flow. The first two pipes operating simultaneously fill the tank in the same time during which the tank is filled by the third pipe alone. The second pipe fills the tank 5 hours faster than the first pipe and 4 hours slower than the third pipe. The time required by the first pipe is:
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: Suppose, first pipe alone takes x hours to fill the tank . Then, second and third pipes will take (x -5) and (x - 9) hours respectively to fill the tank. 1 + 1 = 1 x (x - 5) (x - 9) x - 5 + x = 1 x(x - 5) (x - 9) (2x - 5)(x - 9) = x(x - 5) x2 - 18x + 45 = 0 (x - 15)(x - 3) = 0 x = 15. [neglecting x = 3]

Pipes and Cistern.question: 6. Two pipes can fill a tank in 20 and 24 minutes respectively and a waste pipe can empty 3 gallons per minute. All the three pipes working together can fill the tank in 15 minutes. The capacity of the tank is:
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: Work done by the waste pipe in 1 minute = 1 - 1 + 1 15 20 24 = 1 - 11 15 120 = - 1 . [-ve sign means emptying] 40 Volume of 1 part = 3 gallons. 40 Volume of whole = (3 x 40) gallons = 120 gallons.

Pipes and Cistern.question: 7. A tank is filled in 5 hours by three pipes A, B and C. The pipe C is twice as fast as B and B is twice as fast as A. How much time will pipe A alone take to fill the tank?
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: Suppose pipe A alone takes x hours to fill the tank. Then, pipes B and C will take x and x hours respectively to fill the tank. 2 4 1 + 2 + 4 = 1 x x x 5 7 = 1 x 5 x = 35 hrs.

Pipes and Cistern.question: 8. Two pipes A and B together can fill a cistern in 4 hours. Had they been opened separately, then B would have taken 6 hours more than A to fill the cistern. How much time will be taken by A to fill the cistern separately?
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: Let the cistern be filled by pipe A alone in x hours. Then, pipe B will fill it in (x + 6) hours. 1 + 1 = 1 x (x + 6) 4 x + 6 + x = 1 x(x + 6) 4 x2 - 2x - 24 = 0 (x -6)(x + 4) = 0 x = 6. [neglecting the negative value of x]

Pipes and Cistern.question: 9. Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 and 30 minutes respectively. If both the pipes are used together, then how long will it take to fill the tank?
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: Part filled by A in 1 min = 1 . 20 Part filled by B in 1 min = 1 . 30 Part filled by (A + B) in 1 min = 1 + 1 = 1 . 20 30 12 Both pipes can fill the tank in 12 minutes.

Pipes and Cistern.question: 10. Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 15 minutes and 20 minutes respectively. Both the pipes are opened together but after 4 minutes, pipe A is turned off. What is the total time required to fill the tank?
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: Part filled in 4 minutes = 4 1 + 1 = 7 . 15 20 15 Remaining part = 1 - 7 = 8 . 15 15 Part filled by B in 1 minute = 1 20 1 : 8 :: 1 : x 20 15 x = 8 x 1 x 20 = 10 2 min = 10 min. 40 sec. 15 3 The tank will be full in (4 min. + 10 min. + 40 sec.) = 14 min. 40 sec.

Pipes and Cistern.question: 11. One pipe can fill a tank three times as fast as another pipe. If together the two pipes can fill the tank in 36 minutes, then the slower pipe alone will be able to fill the tank in:
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: Let the slower pipe alone fill the tank in x minutes. Then, faster pipe will fill it in x minutes. 3 1 + 3 = 1 x x 36 4 = 1 x 36 x = 144 min.

Pipes and Cistern.question: 12. A large tanker can be filled by two pipes A and B in 60 minutes and 40 minutes respectively. How many minutes will it take to fill the tanker from empty state if B is used for half the time and A and B fill it together for the other half?
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: Part filled by (A + B) in 1 minute = 1 + 1 = 1 . 60 40 24 Suppose the tank is filled in x minutes. Then, x 1 + 1 = 1 2 24 40 x x 1 = 1 2 15 x = 30 min.

Pipes and Cistern.question: 13. A tap can fill a tank in 6 hours. After half the tank is filled, three more similar taps are opened. What is the total time taken to fill the tank completely?
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: Time taken by one tap to fill half of the tank = 3 hrs. Part filled by the four taps in 1 hour = 4 x 1 = 2 . 6 3 Remaining part = 1 - 1 = 1 . 2 2 2 : 1 :: 1 : x 3 2 x = 1 x 1 x 3 = 3 hours i.e., 45 mins. 2 2 4 So, total time taken = 3 hrs. 45 mins.

Pipes and Cistern.question: 14. Three taps A, B and C can fill a tank in 12, 15 and 20 hours respectively. If A is open all the time and B and C are open for one hour each alternately, the tank will be full in:
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: (A + B)'s 1 hour's work = 1 + 1 = 9 = 3 . 12 15 60 20 (A + C)'s hour's work = 1 + 1 = 8 = 2 . 12 20 60 15 Part filled in 2 hrs = 3 + 2 = 17 . 20 15 60 Part filled in 6 hrs = 3 x 17 = 17 . 60 20 Remaining part = 1 - 17 = 3 . 20 20 Now, it is the turn of A and B and 3 part is filled by A and B in 1 hour. 20 Total time taken to fill the tank = (6 + 1) hrs = 7 hrs.

Pipes and Cistern.question: 15. Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 6 hours. After working at it together for 2 hours, C is closed and A and B can fill the remaining part in 7 hours. The number of hours taken by C alone to fill the tank is:
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: Part filled in 2 hours = 2 = 1 6 3 Remaining part = 1 - 1 = 2 . 3 3 (A + B)'s 7 hour's work = 2 3 (A + B)'s 1 hour's work = 2 21 C's 1 hour's work = { (A + B + C)'s 1 hour's work } - { (A + B)'s 1 hour's work } = 1 - 2 = 1 6 21 14 C alone can fill the tank in 14 hours.

Pipes and Cistern.question: 16. How much time will the leak take to empty the full cistern?I. The cistern is normally filled in 9 hours. II. It takes one hour more than the usual time to fill the cistern because of la leak in the bottom.
options: a) I alone sufficient while II alone not sufficient to answer
b) II alone sufficient while I alone not sufficient to answer
c) Either I or II alone sufficient to answer
d) Both I and II are not sufficient to answer
e) Both I and II are necessary to answer
Pipes and Cistern.answerText: e) Both I and II are necessary to answer
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: I. Time taken to fill the cistern without leak = 9 hours. Part of cistern filled without leak in 1 hour = 1 9 II. Time taken to fill the cistern in presence of leak = 10 hours. Net filling in 1 hour = 1 10 Work done by leak in 1 hour = 1 - 1 = 1 9 10 90 Leak will empty the full cistern in 90 hours. Clearly, both I and II are necessary to answer the question. Correct answer is (E).

Pipes and Cistern.question: 17. How long will it take to empty the tank if both the inlet pipe A and the outlet pipe B are opened simultaneously?I. A can fill the tank in 16 minutes. II. B can empty the full tank in 8 minutes.
options: a) I alone sufficient while II alone not sufficient to answer
b) II alone sufficient while I alone not sufficient to answer
c) Either I or II alone sufficient to answer
d) Both I and II are not sufficient to answer
e) Both I and II are necessary to answer
Pipes and Cistern.answerText: e) Both I and II are necessary to answer
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: I. A's 1 minute's filling work = 1 16 II. B's 1 minute's filling work = 1 8 (A + B)'s 1 minute's emptying work = 1 - 1 = 1 8 16 16 Tank will be emptied in 16 minutes. Thus, both I and II are necessary to answer the question. Correct answer is (E).

Pipes and Cistern.question: 18. If both the pipes are opened, how many hours will be taken to fill the tank?I. The capacity of the tank is 400 litres.II. The pipe A fills the tank in 4 hours. III. The pipe B fills the tank in 6 hours.
options: c) All I, II and III
d) Any two of the three
e) Even with all the three statements, answer cannot be given.
Pipes and Cistern.solution: Explanation: II. Part of the tank filled by A in 1 hour = 1 4 III. Part of the tank filled by B in 1 hour = 1 6 (A + B)'s 1 hour's work = 1 + 1 = 5 4 6 12 A and B will fill the tank in 12 hrs = 2 hrs 24 min. 5 So, II and III are needed. Correct answer is (B).

Boats and Streams.question: 1. A boat can travel with a speed of 13 km/hr in still water. If the speed of the stream is 4 km/hr, find the time taken by the boat to go 68 km downstream.
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Speed downstream = (13 + 4) km/hr = 17 km/hr. Time taken to travel 68 km downstream = 68 hrs = 4 hrs. 17

Boats and Streams.question: 2. A man's speed with the current is 15 km/hr and the speed of the current is 2.5 km/hr. The man's speed against the current is:
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Man's rate in still water = (15 - 2.5) km/hr = 12.5 km/hr. Man's rate against the current = (12.5 - 2.5) km/hr = 10 km/hr.

Boats and Streams.question: 3. A boat running upstream takes 8 hours 48 minutes to cover a certain distance, while it takes 4 hours to cover the same distance running downstream. What is the ratio between the speed of the boat and speed of the water current respectively?
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Let the man's rate upstream be x kmph and that downstream be y kmph. Then, distance covered upstream in 8 hrs 48 min = Distance covered downstream in 4 hrs. x x 8 4 = (y x 4) 5 44 x =4y 5 y = 11 x. 5 Required ratio = y + x : y - x 2 2 = 16x x 1 : 6x x 1 5 2 5 2 = 8 : 3 5 5 = 8 : 3.

Boats and Streams.question: 4. A motorboat, whose speed in 15 km/hr in still water goes 30 km downstream and comes back in a total of 4 hours 30 minutes. The speed of the stream (in km/hr) is:
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Let the speed of the stream be x km/hr. Then, Speed downstream = (15 + x) km/hr, Speed upstream = (15 - x) km/hr. 30 + 30 = 4 1 (15 + x) (15 - x) 2 900 = 9 225 - x2 2 9x2 = 225 x2 = 25 x = 5 km/hr. Video Explanation: https://youtu.be/lMFnNB3YQOo

Boats and Streams.question: 5. In one hour, a boat goes 11 km/hr along the stream and 5 km/hr against the stream. The speed of the boat in still water (in km/hr) is:
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Speed in still water = 1 (11 + 5) kmph = 8 kmph. 2 Video Explanation: https://youtu.be/KQX_mA3tcVA

Boats and Streams.question: 6. A boat running downstream covers a distance of 16 km in 2 hours while for covering the same distance upstream, it takes 4 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Rate downstream = 16 kmph = 8 kmph. 2 Rate upstream = 16 kmph = 4 kmph. 4 Speed in still water = 1 (8 + 4) kmph = 6 kmph. 2 Video Explanation: https://youtu.be/3D8uAfzz3l0

Boats and Streams.question: 7. The speed of a boat in still water in 15 km/hr and the rate of current is 3 km/hr. The distance travelled downstream in 12 minutes is:
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Speed downstream = (15 + 3) kmph = 18 kmph. Distance travelled = 18 x 12 km = 3.6 km. 60 Video Explanation: https://youtu.be/IDOwWUeOldQ

Boats and Streams.question: 8. A boat takes 90 minutes less to travel 36 miles downstream than to travel the same distance upstream. If the speed of the boat in still water is 10 mph, the speed of the stream is:
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Let the speed of the stream x mph. Then, Speed downstream = (10 + x) mph, Speed upstream = (10 - x) mph. 36 - 36 = 90 (10 - x) (10 + x) 60 72x x 60 = 90 (100 - x2) x2 + 48x - 100 = 0 (x+ 50)(x - 2) = 0 x = 2 mph.

Boats and Streams.question: 9. A man can row at 5 kmph in still water. If the velocity of current is 1 kmph and it takes him 1 hour to row to a place and come back, how far is the place?
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Speed downstream = (5 + 1) kmph = 6 kmph. Speed upstream = (5 - 1) kmph = 4 kmph. Let the required distance be x km. Then, x + x = 1 6 4 2x + 3x = 12 5x = 12 x = 2.4 km.

Boats and Streams.question: 10. A boat covers a certain distance downstream in 1 hour, while it comes back in 1 hours. If the speed of the stream be 3 kmph, what is the speed of the boat in still water?
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Let the speed of the boat in still water be x kmph. Then, Speed downstream = (x + 3) kmph, Speed upstream = (x - 3) kmph. (x + 3) x 1 = (x - 3) x 3 2 2x + 6 = 3x - 9 x = 15 kmph.

Boats and Streams.question: 11. A boatman goes 2 km against the current of the stream in 1 hour and goes 1 km along the current in 10 minutes. How long will it take to go 5 km in stationary water?
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Rate downstream = 1 x 60 km/hr = 6 km/hr. 10 Rate upstream = 2 km/hr. Speed in still water = 1 (6 + 2) km/hr = 4 km/hr. 2 Required time = 5 hrs = 1 1 hrs = 1 hr 15 min. 4 4

Boats and Streams.question: 12. A man can row three-quarters of a kilometre against the stream in 11 minutes and down the stream in 7 minutes. The speed (in km/hr) of the man in still water is:
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: We can write three-quarters of a kilometre as 750 metres, and 11 minutes as 675 seconds. Rate upstream = 750 m/sec = 10 m/sec. 675 9 Rate downstream = 750 m/sec = 5 m/sec. 450 3 Rate in still water = 1 10 + 5 m/sec 2 9 3 = 25 m/sec 18 = 25 x 18 km/hr 18 5 = 5 km/hr.

Boats and Streams.question: 13. Speed of a boat in standing water is 9 kmph and the speed of the stream is 1.5 kmph. A man rows to a place at a distance of 105 km and comes back to the starting point. The total time taken by him is:
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Speed upstream = 7.5 kmph. Speed downstream = 10.5 kmph. Total time taken = 105 + 105 hours = 24 hours. 7.5 10.5

Boats and Streams.question: 14. A man takes twice as long to row a distance against the stream as to row the same distance in favour of the stream. The ratio of the speed of the boat (in still water) and the stream is:
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Let man's rate upstream be x kmph. Then, his rate downstream = 2x kmph. (Speed in still water) : (Speed of stream) = 2x + x : 2x - x 2 2 = 3x : x 2 2 = 3 : 1.

Boats and Streams.question: 15. A man rows to a place 48 km distant and come back in 14 hours. He finds that he can row 4 km with the stream in the same time as 3 km against the stream. The rate of the stream is:
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Suppose he move 4 km downstream in x hours. Then, Speed downstream = 4 km/hr. x Speed upstream = 3 km/hr. x 48 + 48 = 14 or x = 1 . (4/x) (3/x) 2 So, Speed downstream = 8 km/hr, Speed upstream = 6 km/hr. Rate of the stream = 1 (8 - 6) km/hr = 1 km/hr. 2

Boats and Streams.question: 16. A boat takes a total time of three hours to travel downstream from P and Q and upstream back from Q to P. What is the speed of the boat in still water?I. The speed of the river current is 1 km per hour. II. The distance between P and Q is 4 km.
options: a) I alone sufficient while II alone not sufficient to answer
b) II alone sufficient while I alone not sufficient to answer
c) Either I or II alone sufficient to answer
d) Both I and II are not sufficient to answer
e) Both I and II are necessary to answer
Boats and Streams.answerText: e) Both I and II are necessary to answer
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: I. Speed of the current = 1 km/hr. II. PQ = 4 km. Let the speed of the boat in still water be x km/hr. Then, 4 + 4 = 3. This gives x. (x + 1) (x - 1) Correct answer is (E).

Boats and Streams.question: 17. What is the speed of the boat in still water?I. It takes 2 hours to cover the distance between A and B downstream. II. It takes 4 hours to cover the distance between A and B upstream.
options: a) I alone sufficient while II alone not sufficient to answer
b) II alone sufficient while I alone not sufficient to answer
c) Either I or II alone sufficient to answer
d) Both I and II are not sufficient to answer
e) Both I and II are necessary to answer
Boats and Streams.answerText: d) Both I and II are not sufficient to answer
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: Let AB = x km. I. Speed downstream = x km/hr 2 II. Speed upstream = x km/hr. 4 Speed of boat in still water = 1 x + x km/hr. 2 2 4 Thus, I and II both even do not give the answer. Correct answer is (D).

Boats and Streams.question: 18. What is the speed of the boat in still water?I. The boat covers a distance of 48 kms in 6 hours while running upstream. II. The boat covers the same distance in 4 hours while running downstream.
options: a) I alone sufficient while II alone not sufficient to answer
b) II alone sufficient while I alone not sufficient to answer
c) Either I or II alone sufficient to answer
d) Both I and II are not sufficient to answer
e) Both I and II are necessary to answer
Boats and Streams.answerText: e) Both I and II are necessary to answer
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: I. Speed upstream = 48 km/hr = 8 km/hr. 6 II. Speed downstream = 48 km/hr = 12 km/hr. 4 Speed of the boat = 1 (8 + 12) km/hr = 10 km/hr. 2 Thus, I and II together give the answer. Correct answer is (E).

Boats and Streams.question: 19. What is the speed of the boat in still water?I. The speed downstream is 12 kmph.II. The speed upstream is 4 kmph. III. In a to and fro journey between two points, the average speed of the boat was 6 kmph.
options: b) All I, II and III
c) III, and either I or II
d) Any two of the three
Boats and Streams.answerText: d) Any two of the three
Boats and Streams.solution: Explanation: From I and II, speed of boat in still water = 1 (12 + 4) km/hr = 8 km/hr. 2 From II and III, we get: Using average speed = 2xy , we get: 2 x 4 x y = 6 x + y 4 + y 8y = 24 + 6y y = 12. Required speed = 1 (12 + 4) km/hr = 8 km/hr. 2 Similarly, I and III also give the answer. Correct answer is (D).

Alligation or Mixture.question: 1. A vessel is filled with liquid, 3 parts of which are water and 5 parts syrup. How much of the mixture must be drawn off and replaced with water so that the mixture may be half water and half syrup?
Alligation or Mixture.solution: Explanation: Suppose the vessel initially contains 8 litres of liquid. Let x litres of this liquid be replaced with water. Quantity of water in new mixture = 3 - 3x + x litres 8 Quantity of syrup in new mixture = 5 - 5x litres 8 3 - 3x + x = 5 - 5x 8 8 5x + 24 = 40 - 5x 10x = 16 x = 8 . 5 So, part of the mixture replaced = 8 x 1 = 1 . 5 8 5

We have to find x. So, the can contained 21 litres of A.

Races and Games.question: 1. In a 100 m race, A can give B 10 m and C 28 m. In the same race B can give C:
Races and Games.solution: Explanation: A : B = 100 : 90. A : C = 100 : 72. B : C = B x A = 90 x 100 = 90 . A C 100 72 72 When B runs 90 m, C runs 72 m. When B runs 100 m, C runs 72 x 100 m = 80 m. 90 B can give C 20 m.

Races and Games.solution: Explanation: A's speed = 5 x 5 m/sec = 25 m/sec. 18 18 Time taken by A to cover 100 m = 100 x 18 sec = 72 sec. 25 Time taken by B to cover 92 m = (72 + 8) = 80 sec. B's speed = 92 x 18 kmph = 4.14 kmph. 80 5

Races and Games.question: 3. In a 500 m race, the ratio of the speeds of two contestants A and B is 3 : 4. A has a start of 140 m. Then, A wins by:
Races and Games.solution: Explanation: To reach the winning post A will have to cover a distance of (500 - 140)m, i.e., 360 m. While A covers 3 m, B covers 4 m. While A covers 360 m, B covers 4 x 360 m = 480 m. 3 Thus, when A reaches the winning post, B covers 480 m and therefore remains 20 m behind. A wins by 20 m.

Races and Games.question: 4. In a 100 m race, A beats B by 10 m and C by 13 m. In a race of 180 m, B will beat C by:
Races and Games.solution: Explanation: A : B = 100 : 90. A : C = 100 : 87. B = B x A = 90 x 100 = 30 . C A C 100 87 29 When B runs 30 m, C runs 29 m. When B runs 180 m, C runs 29 x 180 m = 174 m. 30 B beats C by (180 - 174) m = 6 m.
